definition: A value you pass into a function when calling it.
A piece of data stored on an object, accessed with dot notation.
example: person.name accesses the name attribute of person.

definition: A value that is either True or False.
A blueprint for creating objects that share structure and behavior.
A function that wraps another function to add behavior without changing its code.
A collection of key-value pairs.
An error that occurs during program execution and can be caught with try/except.
A reusable, named block of code that can take inputs and return a result.
A function that produces a sequence of values lazily, one at a time, using yield.
Anything you can loop over with a for loop, like a list or a string.
An object that produces the next value in a sequence, one at a time, until exhausted.
A small, unnamed function defined in a single expression.
A function that belongs to an object and usually acts on its data.
A single Python file containing code that can be imported elsewhere.
A specific instance created from a class, with its own data.
A folder of modules, marked with an __init__.py file (or implicitly in modern Python).
A named placeholder in a function definition that receives an argument.
example: def greet(name): — name is the parameter.

definition: A function that calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem.
example: def factorial(n): return 1 if n == 0 else n * factorial(n-1)

definition: The region of code where a variable name is accessible.
example: A variable created inside a function isn't visible outside it.

definition: An ordered, immutable collection of values.
A name that refers to a value stored in memory.
